title: Automatic Tracing in Task-Based Runtime Systems
problem: In task-based parallel runtime systems, dependence analysis becomes a performance bottleneck when task granularity is fine, and existing tracing techniques that memoize this analysis require brittle manual annotations by programmers that are difficult to apply to programs built from composing independent library components.
motivation: Task-based programming models are widely used for HPC applications, but manual trace annotation limits adoption and does not scale to complex, multi-library programs where the component author cannot anticipate composition.
method: Apophenia automatically discovers traces in task-based runtime systems through a series of dynamic string analyses applied to the stream of tasks issued by the application. It identifies repeated program fragments online by treating the task stream as a string and detecting periodicity, then memoizes the dependence analysis for those fragments. The system requires no programmer annotation and integrates with existing task-based runtimes by intercepting the task issue API.
key_novelty: Automatic trace discovery via dynamic string periodicity analysis of the task stream, eliminating manual annotation entirely while achieving near-manual-trace performance.
contributions: Apophenia system for automatic trace identification in task-based runtime systems without programmer annotation
Dynamic string analysis algorithms for detecting repeated program fragments in task streams
Demonstration of 0.92x–1.03x performance parity with manually traced programs
Speedups of 0.91x–2.82x over untraced programs on Perlmutter and Eos supercomputers

metrics.speedup: 0.91x–2.82x over untraced programs; 0.92x–1.03x vs. manually traced
metrics.other: evaluated on Perlmutter and Eos supercomputers

limitations: Relies on task stream periodicity; may not generalize to highly irregular or data-dependent task graphs where no repeated pattern exists.
primary_theme: Automatic memoization of task dependence analysis in parallel runtimes
